proposal.title: Campaign timeline — Artemis. A new generation. A familiar way to work.
proposal.reason: Convert this campaign to an independent dated timeline object. Dates are resolved from its execution process without changing precision. Preserve all existing event/subprocess ownership; marketing-step reference_id is absent throughout. Consolidate presentations, campaign material and useful claim-policy requirements into narrated steps; remove historical acceptance labels and duplicate import fragments. Product-owned launch links remain authoritative and validated through the explicit transitional execution mapping. Add the campaign alongside the unchanged execution-process step in process.artemis_development.

before.title: Artemis. A new generation. A familiar way to work.
before.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
claim_policy: status: Accepted campaign plan; demonstrations and performance claims require validation
compatibility policy / announced: 1980-05-19
compatibility policy / supported through: 2000-12-31

compatibility policy / scope: Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path.

compatibility policy / exclusions: Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path.

compatibility policy / delivery requirements: Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. Staffing, funding and validation remain explicit launch readiness gates.
compatibility policy / status: Official scenario commitment at NCC 1980; future fulfilment is not established evidence.

claims / memory: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.

claims / os: Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.

claims / compiler: Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.

claims / applications: Native Abacus 2, Business Tools and qualified independent BPI editions. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
claims / continuity: Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.
launch gates / 0: Measured benchmark and reproducible display comparison
launch gates / 1: Qualified demo memory/process footprint and printing paths
launch gates / 2: Published native/card application matrix and OS licensing status
launch gates / 3: Versioned compatibility policy, engineering owner, staffing and funded maintenance plan
launch gates / 4: Dealer stock/service readiness and Academy instructor qualification

marketing_content.description: Identical vector transformations and fixed-point precision, inputs, rounding and verified output; time computation separately from rendering and I/O. Publish source, compiler options, configuration and repeat-run range.
Same shaded rotating cube, geometry and image quality; identify display hardware, frame-buffer and display-transfer costs separately. Do not infer pure CPU speed from unequal graphics systems.
Publish measured ratios only after reproducible qualification; no forecast assumes an unmeasured speed multiplier.

Incremental qualified 80×40 and 80×25 high-resolution text demonstrations, grayscale bitmap/sprites, explicit old-monitor limitations and replaceable card. Retain existing presentation duration; incorporate into Artemis product demonstration.

before.title: Artemis line development and launch programme
before.description: Coordinate Artemis-line development from the beginning of AIONix exploratory work in February 1978, through confidential CP/M-80 bridge implementation and the NCC 1980 launch campaign and its recorded follow-up. Existing child programmes retain their technical scope, licensing and disclosure limits.

participant.role: AIONix and CP/M compatibility engineering partner

inputs.description: The established computer companies provide the organisation and engineering resources for next-generation platform development.
Build on existing software interfaces and retain a defined migration path while keeping future architecture confidential until NCC 1980.

steps.description: Begin with AIONix exploratory and formal operating-system development.
Develop and validate confidential Artemis components and systems from September 1978 through April 1980, preserving the NCC 1980 architecture-disclosure boundary.
Begin confidential detailed implementation of the optional CP/M-80 compatibility module, distinguishing engineering work from shipment.

Before NCC 1980, qualify partners privately, rehearse dealer demonstrations, pilot porting clinics and conduct embargoed briefings. Public teasers promise a familiar workflow without revealing the architecture or word size.
Execute campaign.ncc1980 through its existing launch and follow-up process, including the Artemis commercial launch.

outcomes.description: Artemis has a recorded commercial launch supported by AIONix development, compatibility engineering and campaign follow-up. The start of bridge implementation alone does not establish a shipped or universally compatible module.
